quote: We should be willing to act as a balm for all wounds.
source: Etty Hillesum, An Interrupted Life, the last diary entry, October 1942 (trans. Arnold J. Pomerans, 1983)
note: The sentence closes the diary as the 1983 selection prints it. In the manuscript a line written in capitals follows it, and the complete edition renders the Dutch as a wish to be a balm on many wounds, so it is not strictly the last sentence of the diaries.

evidence.where: Pantheon 1983 and Holt 1996 scans on archive.org are lending restricted and could not be read; wording confirmed through the British Library European Studies blog (27 January 2025), Philip Knight's paper citing the Eerdmans complete edition, and consistent secondary quotation of the Pomerans translation
evidence.edition: An Interrupted Life: The Diaries of Etty Hillesum 1941 to 1943, trans. Arnold J. Pomerans (Pantheon, 1983)
evidence.locator: final diary entry, October 1942 (dated 10 October by the British Library, 13 October by other sources); Dutch: Men zou een pleister op vele wonden willen zijn

reason: The line is real and is the last sentence of the diaries as Pomerans's 1983 selection prints them, but the proposal called it the closing sentence of the diaries outright; Knight, citing the complete edition, reports a further capitalised line on the last page. The locator is narrowed to the last entry. Hillesum is at two of three; nothing shipped.
